newsitem.title: GERMANY: Puma sees 1997 sales rise below 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Puma sees 1997 sales rise below 10 pct.

text.p: German sportswear group Puma AG said on Friday it expected sales growth below 10 percent this year after turnover climbed six percent in the first half.
"Overall we are expecting single-digit rate sales growth for the 1997 business year," the company said in an interim statement.
Puma said its sales reached 275.7 million marks in the first six months of the year and net profit advanced 6.1 percent to 41.2 million marks.
Orders in hand on June 30 were up 18.8 percent at 205.7 million marks, Puma said, with sports shoes accounting for a 13.2 percent rise, textiles for 32.4 percent and accessories for 58 percent.

But despite good orders, delays related to the start up of a new logistical centre in Germany slowed sales in May and June, the company said, and the effect would probably continue into the third quarter.
European sales in the first half, affected by the slowdown, were 185.1 million marks while Asia-Pacific sales rose 14.4 percent to 35.9 million marks.
American sales rose to 47.8 million marks from 34.6 million marks, mainly due to positive developments in Canada and a joint venture company in Chile. Sales in the U.S. were flat, Puma said.
